title: Potential outcomes
dek: Each unit has Y(1) and Y(0). You observe one. Causal effects are comparisons of those two, not coefficients from a convenience regression.
story: Write two random variables per person: Yᵢ(1) if treated (new regimen, vaccine, community A), Yᵢ(0) if not. The individual effect is Yᵢ(1) − Yᵢ(0). You never see both. The fundamental problem of causal inference is missing data with a structure, not a GLM complaint.

SUTVA (stable unit treatment value): one version of treatment, and no interference — your neighbour’s treatment does not write your Y(1). TB transmission studies violate interference constantly. Then the potential outcome needs a richer index (who else was treated).

Assignment mechanism: the law of Zᵢ given covariates and potential outcomes. Randomisation makes Z independent of (Y(0),Y(1)). Observational studies replace that with a modelled ignorability claim: (Y(0),Y(1)) ⊥ Z | X. That claim is not granted by putting X in a logit.
deepTitle: ATE, ATT, and what a coefficient is
deep: ATE = E[Y(1) − Y(0)]. ATT = E[Y(1) − Y(0) | Z=1]. These differ when treatment effects are heterogeneous and treatment is selective. A randomised trial with full compliance estimates an ATE for the trial population, not for the country.

Under randomisation, the difference in means is unbiased for the ATE (plus SUTVA). Under ignorability and overlap, a correctly specified outcome regression, weighting by propensity scores, or a doubly robust mix can target the ATE. Overlap: if some X has P(Z=1|X) = 0 or 1, you have no empirical counterfactual there.

A logit of “outcome on treatment plus covariates” estimates a conditional association. It equals a causal log odds ratio only extra assumptions (no unmeasured confounding, correct mean, no interference, consistency of the treatment variable). Write those, or write “association.”

Instrumental variables, difference-in-differences, and regression discontinuity are other assignment stories. They are not in this plate. Do not paste a DAG from a book; draw the assignment you actually had.

formulas.label: ATE
formulas.note: A mean of missing contrasts. Identification needs an assignment assumption.

formulas.label: Consistency / observation rule
formulas.note: You see the potential outcome corresponding to the treatment actually taken.

visual.caption: For three schematic units, both potential outcomes exist as bars; the faded bar is the one you did not see. The causal contrast is the pair, not the observed Y alone. Unit 3’s missing Y(1) is why you need an assignment story, not another covariate in silence.

example.title: A new shorter regimen, incomplete observation
example.setup: Z = 1 if assigned a 6-month regimen. Y = 1 if relapse-free at 12 months. Some patients in the control arm take the new drugs privately (noncompliance). Some households share treatment (interference).

steps.title: Name Y(z)
steps.body: Even before data, write Y(1), Y(0). If interference matters, write Yᵢ(z_i, z_{−i}) and admit the ATE as first defined is not the scientific object.

steps.title: Assignment
steps.body: If Z was randomised at patient level, ITT contrasts E[Y | Z=1] − E[Y | Z=0] still has a design-based reading as an effect of assignment, not of ingestion.

steps.title: Do not quietly switch estimands
steps.body: Per-protocol OLS among compliers is closer to an ATT-like object with selection. It needs a new identification sentence, not the randomisation sentence.

example.takeaway: Write the missing potential outcomes, the interference claim, and the assignment. Then choose an estimator.

check.prompt: The fundamental problem of causal inference is:
choices: That for each unit you observe at most one of Y(1), Y(0)
check.answer: That for each unit you observe at most one of Y(1), Y(0)
check.why: Missing counterfactuals. OLS bias is a later, optional problem.

check.prompt: Three units with observed Y: treated 8, control 5, treated 2. You cannot compute the ATE from these three numbers alone because:
choices: the missing Y(0)s and Y(1)s are not in the list — 8,5,2 are not a complete pair of potential outcomes
check.answer: the missing Y(0)s and Y(1)s are not in the list — 8,5,2 are not a complete pair of potential outcomes
check.why: Difference of observed means needs an assignment assumption to equal an ATE. The raw three numbers are not even that difference yet without grouping, and grouping still leaves missing counterfactuals.

whyWrong.ATE is a Bayesian object: ATE is a functional of potential outcomes.
whyWrong.SUTVA forbids means: SUTVA is about versions and interference.
